episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. We not only cover football & basketball, but we dive into recruiting, baseball, soccer, and more. For insight that you can't get anywhere else, tune into 103.9/ 98.3 FM. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.

transcript_window.text: And the added wrinkle in all this is that with all the conferences going to nine conference games, you know, you look at a 12 game schedule.
If you've got nine and then let's say you have a rivalry game outside of that, you know, 10 of your games are already locked down.
The other two, you're probably going to want to get a guarantee game and you're maybe going to want to play a lower level game.
So you have to navigate all these pieces and find just the right team.
And with Auburn, it's good example where we were able to find a game they were already going to host at home.
And in essence, what we did was talk to them and say, let's move this to Atlanta because it helps us create some NIL benefit for their players.
It gives them a higher profile stage to play the opening game on.
Their kids get to play in an NFL stadium.
But it's not as easy as it used to be anywhere, anytime.

time yeah now every coach is saying god you know i don't want to play a school that has a ton of oil money and can backfill their nil i don't want to play a team that if i lose to them it's going to hurt me when the cfp starts looking at my resume so uh it's not impossible but it's definitely

a lot more complicated than it used to be yeah and so that being said that it's it's it's complex complex it's nuanced it's you're trying to create these incentive structures to help build up hopefully their resumes right and so you you know like i i find it very intriguing because i

chatted with brett yormark last year i was like look like i see it coming i see what the sec is doing i see what you know some of these especially the sec they want to be able to leverage in my my opinion, from looking from afar, their equity that they've built up over 25 years, and we're only going to play ourselves, and
we're in a gauntlet, and Sankey will tell you at the end of the season, we went through a gauntlet, and we deserve nine teams in the college football playoff.

He's going to make that pitch because he's the commissioner for it, and the Big Ten's going to do it, know, Petitti and everybody else is going to do the same thing with their nine conference games, and as a consumer, as a media member, we're all looking at it as, no, no, we want more data points, The four that you've
mentioned, including the athlete, I love that these are still occurring.
And we need more of it.
I don't know what the path is forward in order to incentivize or restructure.
You had mentioned the NFL light or this NFL minor league, if you will.
But you have to be able to execute some of these P4 versus P4 games in the preseason.
You can't do it midseason because at the end of season, those are conference games.
So we've got to figure out more of these situations.
How do we do that is the question.
There's no doubt.

And we've tried to take an innovative approach to that with the NIL, saying that if we could take a team like Auburn and for their student -athletes, utilize their student -athletes to help us promote ticket sales, promote television viewership, promote the events to their fans, And it gives us a chance to
support the student athlete in a way that they were not able to do it previously.
Obviously, that helps the schools.
